chapter: Savoy days, the Concord and business
title: Managers, accountant and no exploitation
summary: He had only one manager, Moe Gale, and a long-time accountant, and gave Christmas bonuses.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: What kind of, from the business end, what kind of experiences have you had with managers, and agents, and other people that are business men as opposed to being musicians because many musicians have had, you know, negative dealins as a result of the different approaches taken by artists and business people? Have you had any of those kinds of unfortunate circumstances?
No. I wasn't in too much trouble that way. After I got my first personal manager, I only had one personal manager, and that was Moe Gale. And, he treated me like his son.
I had an accountant that came in. And, he still, that's in the 40's, and he's still taking care of my books.
Same accountant. And he's just like a father to me. He's in his 80's now. I think he's gonna retire pretty soon. He
has let a lot of people go except me and a couple others.

So, I've been fortunate enough in that part not to be in too much of that kind of dirty dealing and all that. From the office, Christian was down in the office, down to the booking office I was in, and Moe Gale was there to overlook everything that was being carried on for me.

So, we was something like, well, just like I said like partners, like at Christmas, the band, the fellows there, every Christmas I had a nice bonus for them for Christmas. You know, things like that made them like a family.

I guess that's the reason why I'm fortunate enough to go through as long as I did. You know? Cause like you said, I've heard that too, about a lot of different things concerning different organizations. You may get hold to the wrong person. They didn't get along whoever they

had, you know.
So, I kind of looked towards that.
I didn't want to get into that. And, I want to believe in somebody if we work together. If I play with somebody and don't think we can get along, I'd rather not cause I don't like headaches. I like the things to go along cause they can depend on me. If I say I'm gonna do something for you and work, I work. And then, you won't have no trouble with me. But, if you turn around and do something that I don't, I won't care for, I'd rather not, I'd rather go look for somebody. I think I went through I think maybe a couple that told me, they said I don't, I won't go back there no more. And, that's about all.
So, by and large, you were able to stay away from or get around, you know, that syndrome of being exploited by agents and managers and club owners and things of that sort.
Like I didn't have but one. And so, he was the one.
At that time, and he was with me until not too long before I came in here, till he passed.
So, I was fortunate enough in that part.
